subject: Private telemetry: mTLS streaming + backpressure plan for SIEM parity
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <security@northstar.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private telemetry – requirements and parity questions

Hi Soojin / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We started a security review and have two main asks before we sign off on the Private deployment plan: 1) we need telemetry parity with our existing Splunk SIEM (events + traces + alert fidelity), and 2) telemetry transfer must meet our network safety rules (mTLS, mutual cert rotation, and a disk-backed local buffer for backpressure).

Attached is a short spec (ns_telemetry_spec_v1.pdf) that lists the event categories and retention expectations. A couple of clarifying questions:

- Can Redwood support OTLP/gRPC with mTLS from an on-prem forwarder to a customer-managed HEC endpoint?
- If you require a forwarder component in our VPC, can it provide disk-backed buffering and bounded memory queues to avoid data loss during bursts?
- What's your suggested approach for cert rotation and key custody for mTLS mutual auth?

We'd like a brief runbook + checklist we can share with our platform team. Can you respond with a proposed pattern and the runbook you recommend?

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Private telemetry – requirements and parity questions

Alex — thanks for the spec, that's helpful. High level answers up front: yes, we can support OTLP/gRPC with mTLS; yes, we recommend a lightweight forwarder in-customer-VPC (container or VM) that handles buffering, batching and compression; and for cert rotation we support either customer-managed PKI with short-lived client certs or an automated ACME-based flow with an HSM-backed root.

Proposed pattern (summary):
- Deploy a Redwood forwarder (container) inside your telemetry VPC; it exposes a small local HTTP socket for apps and accepts syslog/Fluentd/OTLP.
- Forwarder exports to the customer's SIEM endpoint via OTLP/gRPC or Splunk HEC using mTLS.
- Forwarder has disk-backed buffer (configurable max-size, default 10GB) and backpressure hooks: when upstream HEC is slow, it will persist to disk and apply rate-limited retries.
- Observability parity: we map event fields 1:1, sample traces at configurable rates, and maintain span/kid correlation headers so you can rehydrate alerts.

Security notes:
- Mutual TLS: we recommend customer-issued certs for the forwarder identity; Redwood validates server certs for SIEM endpoints. Cert rotation can be automated via a small rotation agent that calls your ACME or internal CA and writes to the forwarder's keystore.
- Auditing: forwarder writes an append-only audit log locally and ships signed delivery receipts to Redwood's control plane (metadata only) for troubleshooting — no raw PII leaves your VPC unless explicitly allowed.

I'll drop a concise runbook draft in the next message (it includes the commands, config snippets, and cert rotation checklist).

— Soojin

Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex / team — adding a few operational details that often come up during onboarding: 

- Buffer sizing guidance: for customers with bursty traffic we recommend disk-buffer = peak_tokens_per_minute * 2 hours * average_event_size. We'll attach a spreadsheet to help size.
- Backpressure semantics: forwarder supports three modes — drop-oldest, pause-ingress (signals upstream via standard interrupt), and spill-to-object-store (S3/GCS). Default is pause-ingress + disk buffer.
- Retention & indexing: we will publish the event-to-SIEM mapping template (we've done this as a Splunk CIM-compatible mapping) so your correlation search rules don't break.
- Cert rotation: define an owner in your platform team and schedule automated rotation every 30 days for client certs; server certs follow your normal CA cadence. Redwood can accept signed CSR if you want to control keys.

I'll attach a short runbook draft (runbook_mtls_backpressure.docx) and a sample fluentd config snippet. Marissa, can you include the config snippets?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park

Alex — added the runbook and a minimal PoC checklist. Key items in the doc:

1) PoC footprint: single-node forwarder container + sample app traffic generator.
2) Config snippets (fluentd -> OTLP/gRPC with mTLS; syslog-ng -> HEC over mTLS).
3) Operational checks: verify disk watermark thresholds, health probes, and audit receipt delivery to control plane.
4) Troubleshooting: how to recover from full-disk buffer (rotate, ship to object-store, or increase retention window).

Next steps we propose:
- 1-week PoC in your staging VPC (we'll provide the forwarder image and sample configs).
- Provide RBAC template for the rotation agent (we recommend a dedicated service account with certificate-signing permissions).
- Joint run-through with your SIEM team to validate event mappings and detection parity.

Attached: runbook_mtls_backpressure.docx (final draft).

Thanks — ping when you have a preferred PoC start date.
